strengths: Evidence is mandatory on every status change (mcp.php lines 377 and 414, minLength 10) and topic_changes is append-only with session_id stamping (store.php lines 138-146, 275-288). The live record shows this working: every 2 Sep change names the question, the score and the date.

'Never promote two levels in one session. Never promote on a single question.' (gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md line 81) is followed scrupulously in the live trail: N4, N10 and N15 each carry 'One question only, so no promotion'; A17 carries '20 days after securing on 13 Aug, one day short of the three-week spacing rule'. Do not loosen this.
'Ageing: ... Report the flag; do not demote without evidence' (SKILL.md lines 79-80). The queue flags, a human or the adjudicator decides. Keep it.

Practice never moves a status (mcp.php line 1830, README 'A drill is not an attempt'). A bad game day cannot touch her topic chips. This is the right side of the line for an ADHD learner and should survive any change to the queue.

blanks is a real column on attempt_papers (store.php line 100), surfaced on tracker_list_attempts and tracker_get_attempt, and named as the maths behavioural metric in references/subjects/maths.md. It is the one behaviour the system counts, and it is the one that fell from 27 of 39 marks lost (3F, Jul 2026) to zero (19 Aug exit check). That is the precedent for finding 1.

One opening call: tracker_review_queue returns gaps, ageing secures, loose ends, resources and the last session's next_steps together (mcp.php lines 899-992), and the tutor skill opens every session with it. The session never starts from memory.

next_steps as a resume pointer works: session 3's 'Planned next: Resume at practice Q4 ...' is exactly what an unfinished ADHD session needs on the next open. Findings 4 and 9 build on it rather than replace it.

Per-question topic_ref with the reconciliation check (mcp.php tracker_log_attempt, 'The questions on ... add up to ... but the paper is recorded as') turns a paper into a reteach list; attemptTopicBreakdown orders by marks lost. Keep.
Sessions and practice runs are voided, never deleted; practice ingest is idempotent on client_run_id (store.php addPracticeRun). The chart she likes cannot grow phantom spikes from a retry.

Watch notes are written as next actions ('Ask one bare triangle-area question', 'One starter question undoing a cube, then one undoing a square'), not diagnoses. Whatever finding 9 changes about storage, keep that voice.

The README's stance ('Nothing on the board counts consecutive days or withholds anything for missing one') is respected everywhere in the schema: no streak, no last-active, no per-day count exists. Findings 1 and 6 add counts for the tutor and parent only and say so.

findings.title: Cross-topic habits (working not shown, answer-targeting, unfinished, blanks) need a first-class, countable home
findings.where: store.php lines 128-136 (sessions table) and 51-65 (topics.watch); mcp.php lines 388-424 (tracker_log_session schema); gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md 'Progress reports' step 4 (lines 166-168); references/subjects/maths.md 'Behavioural metric'
findings.problem: On 2 Sep 'working not shown' was recorded in four places, each as free text against a topic where it is not a topic problem: A17 evidence ('answer only with no working, despite working being asked for'), R9 ('Division line 45 ÷ 0.8 not written down'), A9-A10 ('the rearranged line y = 3x − 4 was not written down first') and the session summary ('Answers were submitted without working despite working being requested on two questions'). Answer-targeting exists only in the summary ('Q3 correct for all three colours when only the blues were asked for — the recurring answer-targeting habit'). Unfinished questions exist only in P2-P3's watch note ('Practice Q4 ... and Q5 ... were never submitted'). 'Reports the arithmetic in prose rather than writing numbers into the tree boxes' is a 'Coaching flag' inside session 2's summary. Nothing can count any of them, trend them, or show them on the dashboard. The one behaviour with a column, attempt_papers.blanks, is the one that went from 27/39 marks lost to zero. The skill's report step asks for 'The behavioural metric, where the subject has one' — singular, and read out of prose.
findings.why_it_matters: These habits are where marks go regardless of topic status: a secure topic answered without working scores the answer mark only, and answer-targeting loses marks on questions she can do. They are the attention and impulsivity signature of the learner, not of any topic, and the blanks precedent inside this record shows that counting one per sitting and reporting it is what moved it. A tutor that cannot count them cannot tell whether 'what's one thing you could write down?' is working, and the parent cannot see it.
findings.proposal: Migration step 4 (store.php: SCHEMA_VERSION 3 → 4 at line 234; new `if ($v === 4)` branch after line 343, guarded with hasColumn like step 1): `ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN habits TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'` — JSON, the same pattern as practice_run.metrics. Code-side registry in practice.php style: HABIT_KEYS = working_not_shown, answer_targeting, blank_left, unfinished, prose_not_boxes, skip_requested, each with a display name. Tool change, tracker_log_session: optional `habits`: array of { key (enum), lapses (int ≥ 0), held (int ≥ 0), note? (≤ 120 chars) } — `held` is counted so the record is not deficit-only ('working shown on 6 of 8' is the same fact as '2 lapses'). Description line to add: 'habits[]: counts per habit this session, lapses and held. One number each, no prose.' Read side: tracker_review_queue prints one line for the tutor over the last 5 non-void sessions, e.g. 'Habits (last 5 sessions): working shown 9 held / 4 lapses; answered as asked 12 / 1; finished 14 / 2'; tracker_history and /s/{slug}/session/{id} show the row; the dashboard shows the same five-session line to the parent, never a streak. Rewrite SKILL.md step 4 to: 'The behavioural metrics: blanks per paper from attempts, and the habit counts from sessions (working shown, question answered as asked, questions finished, blanks in practice). Report each as held/lapses over the last five sessions and whether lapses are falling. Where a subject has none of these failure modes (speaking, orals), say which metric replaces them.' Upgrade path if events later need to hang off attempts or practice runs too: a habit_event table keyed by session_id / attempt_id / practice_run_id — not needed now.
findings.evidence_needed: self-monitoring and performance feedback for academic task behaviours in ADHD (showing working, completing items, omissions); that measured-and-reported omissions fall — the in-record blanks result is the local evidence

findings.title: Replace the single 8-week ageing rule with a per-topic expanding schedule (next_due, interval_days, outcome) that covers Developing topics and lapses
findings.where: mcp.php lines 899-992 (tracker_review_queue), specifically 909-918 (ageing), 920 (loose ends), 921-922 (gaps); store.php lines 1455-1466 (weeksSince) and 691-725 (updateTopicStatus); gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md 'Status rules' lines 74-80; dashboard.php lines 271-283
findings.problem: The queue's only schedule is: `if ($t['status'] === 'secure' || $t['status'] === 'examready') { $w = weeksSince($t['last_touched']); if ($w === null || $w >= $weeks)` with $weeks defaulting to 8. One interval, the same for secure and examready, no expansion, no record of whether the last touch passed or failed. Developing topics have no schedule at all — they surface only if someone wrote a watch note. Live consequence today: N6-N7, R10, G4-G6 and G9-G12 are Developing, last touched 2026-06-30 (9 weeks), carry no watch note, and appear nowhere in the queue. A demotion removes a topic from the ageing group (A4 is now Developing), so a failed retrieval makes a topic less visible to the scheduler, not more. The 3-week exam-ready spacing lives only in the skill ('passes a spaced re-test ≥3 weeks after going secure ... Check the date with tracker_history') and is enforced by Claude doing date arithmetic by hand — A17's evidence: '20 days after securing on 13 Aug — one day short of the three-week spacing rule'. The 13 loose ends are unordered and mix 'retest a sub-skill' (A5, A8) with 'resume unfinished practice' (P2-P3) and 'never taught' (A9-A10).
findings.why_it_matters: Eight months of retention with ADHD is a spacing problem, and the current model can only say '8 weeks old', and only for secure topics. An expanding schedule keeps the early, fragile review close (3 weeks — already the skill's own rule) and the mature ones far, brings a lapsed topic back sooner instead of dropping it, and gives the four invisible Developing topics a date. It also removes a manual date calculation from every exam-ready decision.
findings.proposal: Migration step 4 columns: `topics.next_due TEXT`, `topics.interval_days INTEGER`, `topic_changes.outcome TEXT` (values taught | pass | fail | note). Interval table as a constant, mapping exactly onto the existing thresholds so this is a formalisation not a new policy: taught → 7 days; pass while developing → 7 → 14; on reaching secure → 21 (the exam-ready re-test date); pass at ≥ 21 → examready, 42; pass → 84; capped at subject.exam_date − 14 days; fail → 7 days and finding 3's lapse rule. tracker_log_session updates[] gains optional `outcome` (enum, default note); updateTopicStatus sets next_due = date + interval only for taught/pass/fail. Queue output becomes: 'Due for retrieval' (next_due ≤ today, earliest first, any status, with days overdue), 'Resume' (last session's next_steps, already printed), 'Priority gaps', 'Next to start' (finding 6), then loose ends as notes only. ageing_weeks stays as the fallback for rows with null next_due. Backfill in step 4 so nothing jumps on deploy: secure/examready → next_due = last_touched + 56 days, interval 56 (today's behaviour); developing → next_due = last_touched + 14, interval 14 (the four invisible topics appear as 7 weeks overdue, which is the truth). Add to the queue line for a secure topic: 'eligible for exam-ready from 2026-09-03' so the adjudicator reads a date instead of computing one. SKILL.md line 74-76 rewrite: 'secure → examready: passes the retrieval the queue schedules 3 weeks after securing (the queue prints the eligible-from date; a pass before it counts as evidence, not promotion).'
findings.evidence_needed: spacing effect and expanding-interval retrieval schedules in mathematics; retention over months in adolescents with ADHD

findings.title: Demotion is asymmetric with promotion: one starter item can demote, and examready can fall two levels on one question
findings.where: gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md 'Status rules' lines 77-78 and 81; dashboard.php line 282; maths-tutor-session SKILL.md line 60 and Update Block line 115 ('Aging flags: secure topics that failed the starter')
findings.problem: Current text: '**Demotion:** a secure/examready topic failed in a starter or check → `developing`, with a note saying what failed.' and, on the dashboard, 'If one fails in a starter, demote it to developing.' Against: 'Never promote two levels in one session. Never promote on a single question.' Promotion needs about four items at 80% unaided plus a three-week wait; demotion needs one starter item, and from examready it drops two levels (examready → developing skips secure) on that one item. A4 was demoted on one item, 3(2x−5) − 2(x+4); the adjudicator justified it from history ('Third wobble on the same sub-skill since going secure on 13 Aug') but the rule as written did not ask for that. The parts of the rule set that are sound and must not change: never two levels up, never on one question, ageing flags without demotion, practice never moves status.
findings.why_it_matters: ADHD performance varies day to day and within a session; the A4 item was in the second full session of a double day. A one-item demotion turns that noise into a status change she can see on her topic chips, and re-promotion then needs an exit-ticket-scale check — a week of work to undo one sign slip. Recording the lapse and shortening the interval keeps the record honest without the status swinging.
findings.proposal: Replace SKILL.md lines 77-78 with: '**Lapse:** a secure/examready topic failed in a starter or check → record it (evidence, `outcome: fail`), keep the status, set `watch` to what failed, and bring the next retrieval forward to within a week. **Demotion** to the level below needs one of: a second fail on the topic within 6 weeks, two or more items wrong in one check, or a fail where the answer was left blank. Demote one level only — `examready` falls to `secure`, never straight to `developing`.' Replace dashboard.php line 282 text with: 'If one fails in a starter, retest it within a week; a second fail demotes it.' Add to maths-tutor-session line 60: 'One failed item is a lapse to record, not a demotion to propose.' A4's demotion stands under the new rule (three wobbles in three weeks), so no correction to the live record is needed.
findings.evidence_needed: intra-individual performance variability in ADHD (day-to-day and time-on-task), and the reliability of single-item assessment

findings.title: Sessions store nothing about time: no duration, start time, shape, how it ended, or hints; practice runs have duration but no link to the session
findings.where: store.php lines 128-136 (sessions) and 1095-1109 (addSession); mcp.php lines 388-424 (tracker_log_session schema) and 641-714 (tracker_log_practice; duration_seconds at 686); practice.php line 38 (maths_session declares hints_used); maths-tutor-session SKILL.md Update Block lines 110-118
findings.problem: sessions holds date, summary, topics_touched, next_steps, void_reason. The fallback Update Block, used only when the connector is down, captures 'Session type: [A/B/C/D] | Duration: ~[x] min' (line 111) — so the skill's authors considered these worth keeping, and the tool that replaced the block drops both. practice_run has duration_seconds and the maths_session source declares a hints_used metric, but practice_run has no session_id, so a tutoring session and its practice run are two rows about the same 90 minutes with no join. Live: two full sessions were logged on 2 Sep; the second is the one where 'Q4 and Q5 were not submitted before the session ended' — whether it was late, long, or simply the second, is unrecoverable.
findings.why_it_matters: Duration, time of day and whether sessions finish are the variables a parent can actually change for an ADHD learner; every other column records what she knows. Without them the record cannot answer 'do 90-minute blocks finish?', 'does the second session of a day go worse?', or 'how many hints did today need?', and the tutor cannot size a starter to the time she has.
findings.proposal: Migration step 4: `ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN shape TEXT` (A | B | C | D | other), `duration_minutes INTEGER`, `started_at TEXT` (HH:MM, local), `ended TEXT` (finished | ran_out | stopped_early | break), `hints_used INTEGER`; `ALTER TABLE practice_run ADD COLUMN session_id INTEGER`. Tool changes: tracker_log_session accepts all five as optional with the description line 'Optional shape, duration_minutes, started_at, ended, hints_used — one word or number each; they are what make sessions comparable.'; tracker_log_practice run objects accept optional session_id (the tutor skill logs practice after tracker_log_session returns the id). Read side: tracker_history prints '90 min, 16:30, ran out' after the date; the dashboard's sessions-by-week shows duration and an ended glyph; tracker_practice_stats can then report hints per session. Follow-on once data exists: tracker_review_queue(minutes?) sizing the retrieval list (3 items for 20 minutes, 5 for 90).
findings.evidence_needed: session length and time-of-day effects on sustained attention and task completion in adolescents with ADHD; effect of hint count as a support-level measure

findings.title: The queue never reads practice, so 'practised in the app, never checked' cannot exist as a state — Spanish reads 1% after four games
findings.where: mcp.php lines 899-992 (tracker_review_queue reads listTopics, listResources, listSessions only) and line 1830; store.php line 1331 (practiceTopicRollup); README 'A drill is not an attempt'; gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md 'Core loop' step 2; references/subjects/spanish.md
findings.problem: Spanish: 100 topics, 2 developing, 98 not started, coverage 1%, while four Shooting Gallery runs at 71-81% accuracy sit in practice_run. Practice never moves a status, which is correct, but the queue never consults practiceTopicRollup either, so the one state most of her Spanish is in — practised repeatedly, never checked — has no representation and generates no next action. The Spanish appendix has no tutoring loop, so a topic stays notstarted until someone remembers to set a check.
findings.why_it_matters: She plays because she likes the chart (README: 'the reason she keeps playing'). The topic model cannot convert that engagement into progress she can see, so the dashboard says 1% after a month. That is exactly the disengagement risk the objective names, and the fix costs no schema change.
findings.proposal: Add a queue group 'Practised, not yet checked': topics with status notstarted or gap whose practiceTopicRollup over the last 28 days shows ≥ 2 runs, ≥ 10 items and ≥ 80% right first time, sorted by accuracy descending, each line e.g. 'T3 Free time — 3 runs, 27 items, 85% first time — set a check (kind: check)'. The adjudicator logs the check and the existing rules move the status. Prerequisite: the Spanish app sends run-level topic_refs on every run (it sends items for misses only) — a one-line change under the language-learning-platform skill. Add to SKILL.md Core loop step 2: 'Practice at ≥ 80% over several runs is evidence that a topic is ready for a check, not evidence for a status.'
findings.evidence_needed: transfer from game-based retrieval practice to tested recall; visible progress as an engagement lever for ADHD learners

findings.title: The queue has no 'next to start' group: 24 not-started maths topics are invisible, and the pace (36 topics in 36 weeks) is never stated
findings.where: mcp.php lines 921-922 and 966-975 (gaps group, heading at 971); topics.sort_order at store.php line 62; maths-tutor-session SKILL.md line 55 ('Teach (30–40 min): the top priority gap from the review queue')
findings.problem: The only teaching group is `$t['status'] === 'gap'`. Twenty-four maths topics are notstarted and never appear. When the 12 gaps are closed the queue prints 'None — no topic is marked as a gap' and the tutor skill has no instruction for what to teach next, although sort_order (spec order) and tier already exist on every topic. The arithmetic the service holds and never prints: 252 days to 2027-05-14 = 36 weeks; 24 notstarted + 12 gap = 36 topics needing first teaching = one per week with no slack for the December, January and February mocks, retests, or Spanish; entries close in 24 weeks.
findings.why_it_matters: For an autonomous ADHD learner the queue is the executive function. If it goes quiet, the session opens with a choice instead of a task, and task initiation is the hard part. The pace line is what tells the parent months early whether the February tier decision is realistic — value to the student comes from decisions being made in time.
findings.proposal: Add group 'Next to start (Foundation first, spec order)': notstarted topics sorted by tier then sort_order, limited to 5, with resources. Add one line at the top of the queue: 'Pace: 36 topics not yet taught, 36 weeks to the exam, entries close in 24 weeks.' — printed to the tutor and on the parent's dashboard beside the countdown badge, never as a student-facing target. Tutor skill line 55 → 'the top priority gap from the review queue, or, if there are none, the first topic under Next to start'.
findings.evidence_needed: none for the arithmetic; for the structure, reducing choice at task start (task initiation) in ADHD

findings.title: The tools invite prose where data belongs: a 2,000-char summary that the queue re-reads in full every session, and an unbounded history
findings.where: mcp.php lines 401-402 (summary: 'What was covered and how it went', maxLength 2000), 987-988 (queue echoes the whole last summary), 322-340 (tracker_history: weeks default 12, no limit); gcse-progress-tracker SKILL.md 'Evidence discipline' lines 106-111; maths-tutor-session SKILL.md line 83
findings.problem: The description 'What was covered and how it went' with a 2,000-character ceiling, plus the skill's 'evidence must let a future reader reconstruct the judgement', produce summaries like session 3's: 1,186 characters (measured) carrying starter scores, the A4 lapse, two behaviour observations and the unfinished questions — all data with nowhere else to go. The queue then echoes the entire summary at every session open (`'Last session logged: ' . $sessions[0]['date'] . ' — ' . $sessions[0]['summary']`), and tracker_history returns every summary for 12 weeks with no limit; at two sessions a week that is around 100 summaries by May. Nothing here pushes long output at the student; the cost is that structured facts are written as prose and read back as prose, and the tutor re-reads 1,200 characters of last time before greeting her.
findings.why_it_matters: Every fact that lives in prose is invisible to the queue, the dashboard and the report. Findings 1, 2 and 4 give those facts columns; this finding stops the prose from filling back up and keeps the session open fast.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the summary description (mcp.php 401-402) to: 'Two to four sentences on what was taught and how it went. Scores go in updates[].evidence, habit counts in habits[], timing in duration_minutes and ended — not here.' Queue echo (line 987): print next_steps in full and the summary cut at 240 characters with '… (session N)'. tracker_history: add `limit` (default 20 sessions) and `brief` (first 160 characters of each summary). Keep the 2,000 cap — lowering it would risk a refused log at the end of a session, which is worse. Tutor skill line 83 already says 'in a sentence or two'; add 'starter scores go in updates, one per topic'.

findings.title: last_touched resets on any write, including corrections, so the retrieval clock restarts without a question being asked
findings.where: store.php lines 691-725 (updateTopicStatus), line 698 (`$touched = $args['last_touched'] ?? gmdate('Y-m-d');`) and 705-708; mcp.php lines 909-918 (ageing reads last_touched)
findings.problem: Every call through updateTopicStatus — evidence-only, watch-only, corrections — sets last_touched to today, and the ageing check reads last_touched. Live: A8 and G14-G16 show last_touched 2026-09-03; both were standalone corrections ('Diagnostic detail recovered from the marked 2F Jun-22 script', 'CORRECTION to the diagnostic record') on a day with no session. Their retrieval clocks restarted although nothing was tested.
findings.why_it_matters: The ageing queue is the only spacing mechanism today; a record-keeping pass silently defers retrieval on every topic it touches. Two topics now, systematic after any bulk correction.
findings.proposal: With finding 2's outcome column: set last_touched only when outcome is taught, pass or fail. Without it: add optional `touched` (boolean, default true) to updates[] and tracker_update_topic, pass false for corrections, and add to SKILL.md 'Correcting the record': 'A correction does not touch the topic — pass touched: false (or last_touched unchanged) so the retrieval clock is left alone.' The two live rows can be fixed by hand with tracker_update_topic last_touched.

findings.title: watch is a single overwritten slot outside the audit trail, and the loose-end group mixes three kinds of note under a heading that misnames them
findings.where: store.php line 59 (topics.watch), line 700 (overwrite on update), lines 138-146 (topic_changes has no watch column); mcp.php line 920 (any non-gap status) and 958 (heading 'Loose ends on secure topics'); dashboard.php lines 259-261
findings.problem: watch is one string per topic, replaced on every update that passes it, and topic_changes does not record it, so the previous loose end is lost — N10's 18 Aug note survives only because the 2 Sep evidence mentions it. The group includes any non-gap status (`$t['watch'] && $t['status'] !== 'gap'`) under 'Loose ends on secure topics': 8 of today's 13 entries are Developing. The bucket mixes 'retest this sub-skill' (A5, A8), 'resume unfinished work' (P2-P3: 'start the next session there') and 'never taught' (A9-A10: 'Schedule a dedicated session'), unordered.
findings.why_it_matters: The resume-point kind is the one that gets her back into an unfinished question fastest; when it sits ninth in an unordered list under the wrong heading it is the easiest thing to skip. For the record, the promise 'Statuses are never rewritten, only appended to' (tracker-service.md) does not cover the note.
findings.proposal: Migration step 4: `ALTER TABLE topic_changes ADD COLUMN watch TEXT`, written alongside each change so tracker_history shows how the note evolved. Heading → 'Loose ends (any status)'. With finding 2, the retest kind is scheduled by next_due and the resume kind lives in session.next_steps, so the group shrinks to notes only; no watch_kind column is needed.

numbers: Weeks to the maths exam: 2027-05-14 minus 2026-09-04 = 252 days; 252 / 7 = 36 weeks. Entries close ~2027-02-21: 170 days / 7 = 24 weeks.
Topics needing first teaching: 24 notstarted + 12 gap = 36; 36 topics / 36 weeks = 1.0 per week with no slack.

Developing topics invisible to the review queue today: N6-N7, R10, G4-G6, G9-G12 = 4 of 12 Developing (no watch note, not secure, not gap); each last touched 2026-06-30 = 66 days = 9 whole weeks. A22 is the fifth 9-week Developing topic and is visible only because it has a watch note.
Loose-end entries today: 13 (N4, N10, N15, A4, A5, A8, A9-A10, A17, A22, R7-R8, G14-G16, P1, P2-P3); 8 Developing + 5 Secure, under a heading that says 'secure topics'.
'Working not shown' on 2 Sep: recorded in 4 places (A17, R9, A9-A10 evidence strings + session 3 summary), 0 of them countable.
Session 3 summary length: 1,186 characters (wc -m on the stored text); echoed in full by tracker_review_queue at every session open.
A17 spacing: secured 2026-08-13, retested 2026-09-02 = 20 days; the 21-day rule was checked by hand in the evidence string.

Schedule comparison from a topic secured on 2026-09-04: current rule (56-day interval, reset on each touch) → 2026-10-30, 2026-12-25, 2027-02-19; proposed 21 → 42 → 84 days → 2026-09-25, 2026-11-06, 2027-01-29. Same number of touches; the proposal puts the first, most fragile one at three weeks and the third before the February tier decision rather than on its deadline week.
Blanks precedent: 27 of 39 marks lost to blanks on 8300/3F (Jul 2026) → 0 blanks on the 19 Aug exit check (22/25); blanks is the only behaviour with a column.

Migration: SCHEMA_VERSION is 3 (store.php line 234); every column proposed above belongs to step 4, one `if ($v === 4)` branch guarded with hasColumn, and /healthz should be extended to name one new column so deploy/smoke-test.sh can assert the step ran.
